statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases to 18% during the 21:00Z-22:00Z futures maintenance halt, when no continuous price discovery exists and the Nasdaq-100 has just closed 1.08% lower but roughly 196 points above a session low that held. Stress stays high at 76% on a ten-year yield reported near 5.24%.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is EA_ON for NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD, with Tail at 18% in the low band. The current clock-hour is the CME maintenance halt from 21:00Z to 22:00Z, so there is no continuous price path that could extend: NQ December last printed 30,556.75 at 20:59:59Z, effectively unchanged from 30,555.25 half an hour earlier. The completed cash session was orderly, with the 30,081.06 low holding and the index recovering about 196 points into the close, so repeated extension after failed retracements was not observed. Stress remains high at 76% because the ten-year yield is reported near 5.24%, its highest since 2007, the thirty-year near 5.56%, crude is elevated with WTI at $93.29, and semiconductors carried an outsized share of the decline. The published danger window stays narrow at 13:30Z to 15:00Z on 29 September, covering the US cash open, JOLTS job openings and CB consumer confidence. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected by the mapped state.
headline: Nasdaq-100 enters the futures maintenance halt after an orderly 1.08% decline; Tail eases to 18% while a semiconductor de-rating keeps Stress high
body: As of the 21:00Z clock-hour the CME equity index maintenance halt is in force until 22:00Z, so no continuous price discovery exists for this slot. The last NQ December print was 30,556.75 at 20:59:59Z, down 1.08% on the day, effectively unchanged from the 30,555.25 observed half an hour earlier in the post-close window and inside a 30,357.75 to 30,920.75 daily range. The cash Nasdaq-100 settled at 30,276.81, down 331.32 points or 1.08% from Friday's 30,608.13, having ranged 30,081.06 to 30,480.40; the close sat close to the middle of that range and roughly 196 points above a low that was set intraday and held, so the decline was an orderly repricing rather than a no-retracement path. The Nasdaq-100 underperformed the broader tape, with the S&P 500 down 0.77% at 7,683.69, the Dow down 0.67% at 51,481.51 and the Nasdaq Composite down 0.92% at 26,820.38. VIX closed at 16.07, up 8.07%, with a 15.68 to 16.62 range: higher on the day but still low in absolute terms. The driver remained rates and energy rather than equity-specific stress. The ten-year yield is reported at 5.24% after a roughly six basis point rise, described as its highest since 2007, and the thirty-year near 5.56%, its highest since 2004; the two-year is reported near 4.92%. The latest published H.15 release still covers 25 September at 4.81% for two years, 5.17% for ten and 5.49% for thirty, so the official series has not yet caught up to today's market levels. WTI is $93.29, up 0.95%, after topping $96.44 intraday and fading as Saudi Arabia restored East-West pipeline flows to roughly 3.5 million barrels a day; Brent is near $106.12, up 1.73%. The sharpest index-level detail this hour is the composition of the decline: Arm fell close to 9%, Qualcomm around 6%, Intel 5.7%, AMD 3.6% and Micron 2.6%, while Nvidia rose 1.68% on a reported $150 billion buyback authorisation and an AI safety platform launch. Reporting attributes the semiconductor move to higher oil prices reviving inflation concerns that compress rate-sensitive valuations, compounded by profit taking in the names that had run hardest, with Arm additionally exposed to a SoftBank margin loan raised to $25 billion. Meta fell about 3.6% to 4.8% after saying its Muse assistant will reach its AI glasses, following a roughly 35% September advance, and MongoDB fell 18.5% after Meta recruited its chief executive. Geopolitically, the Strait of Hormuz has been closed since February and President Trump rejected Iran's roadmap on 26 September, with negotiations reported as possibly resuming this week; crude fading from its intraday peak is consistent with that de-escalation nuance rather than a fresh discontinuity. Tail eases to 18% because the current clock-hour has no tradable price path at all, the completed session retraced, and the amplifier stack is macro and valuation-driven rather than structural. Stress is held high at 76%: a single-session drawdown concentrated in the largest-weight complex is exactly the difficult but recoverable environment the Stress score describes. Confidence is 86%, reflecting verified index, futures, volatility, rates, energy, single-stock and calendar evidence; the limitations are that the shared Finviz context is fresh at about 35 minutes but reported partial with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, that the official H.15 series has not yet published today's values, and that the maintenance halt supplies no live price path into the Globex reopen.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours opened in a calm late-Friday regime with Tail near 11-14% and Stress in the mid 70s, then moved into an overnight repricing that lifted Tail into the 21-24% watch band from the 03:00Z hour as long-end yields extended and crude firmed. Two hours printed in the elevated band: 09:00Z at 26% during the European yield move and 14:00Z at 27% around the US cash open, and each returned to the watch band within an hour rather than extending. Stress climbed from 74% to a peak of 85% at 10:00Z and eased to 77-78% into the close, while Confidence improved from 79% to 88% as the session produced verifiable price-path evidence. Dominant mode rotated from normal through trend-down during the European and early US hours to mixed for the second half of the session.
outlookSummary: The conditional path starts at 18% for the 21:00Z maintenance halt, when no continuous price discovery exists, and stays in the low band at 18-19% through the 22:00Z Globex reopen and the Asian session on an assumption of two-way trade. Tail re-enters the watch band at 20% from the 06:00Z European pre-open and firms to 21-22% through the London open and the 09:00Z hour, the slot that produced today's 26% print. The highest conditional slots are the 13:00Z cash-open window at 22% and the 14:00Z hour at 24%, when JOLTS job openings and CB consumer confidence print together and Stress peaks at 81%. No forecast hour reaches the elevated band, because under this contract event importance and surprise magnitude raise Stress and lower Confidence before they raise Tail, and a higher Tail read would require observed shallow pullbacks, failed retracements or repeated extension that cannot exist in advance. The published danger window is deliberately narrow at 13:30Z to 15:00Z on 29 September. Confidence decays from 86% to 71% across the horizon, and the structural checkpoints beyond it are ADP and core PCE on 30 September and payrolls on 2 October.

forecast.analysis: Globex reopen hour. The first live price path since the halt is the checkpoint: an orderly two-way reopen near the 30,556 settlement area would confirm the low band, while a thin gap that extends without retracement would be the first genuine Tail evidence. Nothing about that structure is observed yet.
